name: David Brown
chief_complaint: Worsening shortness of breath and increased sputum production
opening_statement: I've had COPD for about 8 years now, but over the last 3 days my breathing has gotten much worse. I'm coughing up more phlegm than usual and it's turned green. I'm really struggling to do my normal activities.
emotional_baseline: Anxious but cooperative. Frustrated by declining functional capacity. Concerned about hospitalization.

rag_citations.reference: COPD exacerbation: increased dyspnea beyond normal day-to-day variation (Anthonisen Type 1 criteria)

symptoms.name: Increased sputum production
symptoms.character: Purulent (green), increased volume (from 1 teaspoon to 3 tablespoons daily)

rag_citations.reference: COPD exacerbation: increased sputum purulence (Anthonisen Type 1 criteria)
COPD exacerbation: Anthonisen Type 1 requires all 3 cardinal symptoms (dyspnea, sputum volume, sputum purulence)
COPD exacerbation may present with increased wheeze and airflow obstruction

past_medical_history.complications: 2 exacerbations in past 12 months requiring oral corticosteroids

family_history: Father died age 72 (MI). Mother died age 78 (stroke). Brother has asthma. No family history of lung cancer.

social_history.smoking: 45 pack-year history (started age 18, quit 5 years ago after COPD diagnosis)
social_history.alcohol: Ceased 10 years ago, previously 2 standard drinks daily
social_history.occupation: Retired carpenter (exposed to wood dust for 30 years)
social_history.living_situation: Lives with wife in single-story house, independent ADLs normally

general.appearance: Elderly male, dyspneic at rest, using accessory muscles

respiratory.inspection: Barrel chest, pursed-lip breathing, trachea central, reduced chest expansion
respiratory.auscultation: Diffuse expiratory wheeze, prolonged expiratory phase, reduced air entry bilaterally, scattered coarse crackles in bases

cardiovascular.palpation: Apex beat not displaced, no heaves/thrills
cardiovascular.auscultation: Dual heart sounds, no murmurs, no added sounds, peripheral pulses intact

examination_findings.other: No peripheral oedema, no cyanosis, no clubbing

required.expected_result: pH 7.38, pCO2 48 mmHg, pO2 58 mmHg, HCO3 28 mmol/L (Type 2 respiratory failure, compensated)
Hyperinflation, flattened diaphragms, no consolidation, no pneumothorax
Hb 148 g/L, WCC 12.3 x10⁹/L (neutrophilia 9.2), platelets normal

supportive.expected_result: Sinus tachycardia, no acute ischaemia, P pulmonale
FEV1 58% predicted, FEV1/FVC 0.62 (obstructive pattern, GOLD Stage 2)

expected_management.action: Antibiotic: Doxycycline 100mg BD for 5 days (or Moxifloxacin if severe)
expected_management.rationale: Penicillin allergy, Anthonisen Type 1 exacerbation warrants antibiotics

expected_management.action: Serial ABGs, monitor respiratory rate and SpO2
expected_management.rationale: Assess for worsening hypercapnia or respiratory failure

expected_management.action: Prepare for NIV (BiPAP) if pH <7.35 or rising pCO2 despite treatment
Pulmonary rehabilitation referral, smoking cessation reinforcement, review inhaler technique
expected_management.rationale: Prevent future exacerbations, optimize COPD management

expected_management.action: GP review in 1 week, consider LABA/ICS if ≥2 exacerbations/year
expected_management.rationale: eTG recommends escalation to triple therapy for frequent exacerbators

critical_errors.consequence: May worsen hypercapnia, precipitate CO2 narcosis

critical_errors.error: Amoxicillin prescription despite documented penicillin allergy
Failure to recognize Type 2 respiratory failure (hypoxia + hypercapnia)
critical_errors.consequence: Inappropriate oxygen delivery, missed NIV indication

critical_errors.error: Omitting systemic corticosteroids in Type 1 exacerbation
critical_errors.consequence: Delayed recovery, higher risk of treatment failure

critical_errors.error: Failure to discuss smoking cessation (patient quit 5 years ago)
critical_errors.consequence: Missed opportunity to reinforce cessation (though already quit)

fracp_reviews.credentials: FRACP (Respiratory Medicine), Staff Specialist Royal Prince Alfred Hospital
fracp_reviews.comments: Excellent clinical accuracy. Anthonisen Type 1 criteria correctly applied (all 3 cardinal symptoms present). ABG interpretation and NIV threshold (pH <7.35) aligns with current Thoracic Society guidelines. Antibiotic choice appropriate given penicillin allergy. Critical errors are realistic exam traps (high-flow O2 in COPD, penicillin allergy oversight). Difficulty well-calibrated for medium level - time-critical exacerbation with moderate comorbidity burden.

Scenario mirrors real ED presentations. Social history (retired carpenter, wood dust exposure) adds authenticity. Medication list includes realistic COPD maintenance therapy (tiotropium on PBS restriction). Learning objectives target high-yield concepts (Anthonisen criteria, oxygen targets in Type 2 RF, NIV indications). FRACP candidates should recognize this as straightforward Type 1 exacerbation requiring standard treatment escalation. No concerns for exam use.
fracp_reviews.suggested_changes: None. Approve for AMC clinical exam preparation.

learning_objectives.objective: Apply Anthonisen criteria to classify COPD exacerbation severity
learning_objectives.clinical_relevance: Type 1 (all 3 symptoms) requires antibiotics + corticosteroids per eTG

learning_objectives.objective: Manage Type 2 respiratory failure with controlled oxygen therapy
learning_objectives.clinical_relevance: Target SpO2 88-92% in COPD to prevent CO2 retention

learning_objectives.objective: Recognize indications for Non-Invasive Ventilation (NIV) in COPD
learning_objectives.clinical_relevance: pH <7.35 or rising pCO2 despite treatment warrants BiPAP

learning_objectives.objective: Select appropriate antibiotics for COPD exacerbation in penicillin allergy
learning_objectives.clinical_relevance: Doxycycline or moxifloxacin are eTG-recommended alternatives

learning_objectives.objective: Differentiate COPD exacerbation from heart failure in dyspneic patient
learning_objectives.clinical_relevance: Sputum purulence, wheeze, hyper-resonance favor COPD over HF (which has crackles, dullness, elevated JVP)

learning_objectives.objective: Interpret ABG results in acute COPD exacerbation
learning_objectives.clinical_relevance: Compensated respiratory acidosis (high pCO2, normal pH) indicates chronic CO2 retention

learning_objectives.objective: Prescribe evidence-based corticosteroid regimen for COPD exacerbation
learning_objectives.clinical_relevance: Prednisolone 30-40mg for 5 days reduces treatment failure (eTG guideline)

learning_objectives.objective: Identify patients requiring escalation to triple therapy (LABA/LAMA/ICS)
learning_objectives.clinical_relevance: ≥2 exacerbations/year despite LAMA alone warrants triple therapy per eTG
